title: Ikigami: The Ultimate Limit
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a Japan-like state, a National Prosperity law kills a small share of citizens aged 18 to 24 through capsules given in childhood vaccinations, each warned only 24 hours ahead by a notice called an ikigami. Civil servant Kengo Fujimoto delivers these notices and, story by story, watches how each recipient spends their last day while hiding his own doubts about the law, since open dissent is punished as thought crime.
life_message: Life is precious because it ends, and the last choices a person makes (forgiving, creating, protecting family) show what mattered.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Some recipients answer old humiliations with revenge; the story frames this as tragic, not admirable.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The imposed order and thought-crime arrests are the target of critique.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Final days center on siblings, parents and friends rather than the nation.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Random selection treats all equally, yet officials and politicians exploit it.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Secular, bureaucratic modern state; no religious frame for death.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Recipients choose art, love and reconciliation over productivity.

folkways.japan: Fujimoto's silent compliance as a civil servant reflects Japanese workplace norms of duty and avoiding open dissent, which the story examines.

delivery.evidence: ANN (vol. 4) says it pushes so many moral lessons the meaning gets lost; Manga Bookshelf (vol. 1) found commentary mostly implicit.

personified.character: National Prosperity law and its officials
personified.ideology: Utilitarian state: fear of death makes citizens productive

delivery.note: Each episode closes on a lesson about valuing life; reviewers differ on whether the moralizing is overloaded or carried by character choices.

winners_losers: The recipients' final acts of love and art earn sympathy; the state program is the villain, though citizens who support it are shown as conditioned rather than wicked.
